headline: Carlisle grows above market, raises full-year outlook
summary_short: Carlisle's Q2 2026 revenue rose 8.3% y/y to $1.57B (7.9% organic) on above-market volume growth and re-roofing demand, with continuing-operations diluted EPS up 8% to $6.36, even as Middle East-driven petrochemical and freight cost inflation compressed gross margin to 36.2% from 37.3%.
summary_long: Q2 revenue rose 8.3% y/y (7.9% organic) to $1,570.3M on above-market volume growth, re-roofing demand, and pre-buying ahead of price increases. Gross margin fell to 36.2% from 37.3% as petrochemical and freight cost inflation, driven by Middle East-related oil prices, outpaced April/July price hikes. CWT's adjusted EBITDA margin still rose 380bp q/q on automation and in-house polystyrene capacity gains. Net income was roughly flat at $255.2M as higher interest expense on 2025 notes and a higher tax rate offset operating gains. Carlisle raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to mid-single-digit growth with margins about flat, and lifted its buyback target to $1.2B. Cash fell to $665.3M after $500M of first-half buybacks; long-term debt rose to $2.89B.

drivers.explanation: Above-market volume growth in both segments plus solid re-roofing demand and customer pre-buying ahead of April/July/August price increases; 8.3% reported growth was 7.9% organic.
Grew in dollars but margin fell 110bp to 36.2% as petrochemical raw-material and freight cost inflation from Middle East oil price spikes outpaced Q2 price increases.
Grew with revenue despite margin pressure; CCM held 28.6% operating margin and CWT 10.7%, both 'in line with expectations' even as input costs outpaced pricing realization.
Roughly flat y/y as operating-income gains were offset by $12.7M higher interest expense from 2025 notes issuance and a higher effective tax rate (22.8% vs 21.0%).
Rose mainly on a lower diluted share count (40.5M vs 43.4M y/y) from continued buybacks ($250M repurchased in Q2), even as net income was roughly flat.
Follows the same operating-income drivers; company's own adjusted EBITDA margin was 26.2%, down from 26.9% y/y, as cost inflation outpaced pricing.
